ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit is a series branch from the left-end node a to the right-end node b. On the left side is a resistor labeled 10Ω, and on the right side a 1A current source is connected in series; the arrow beside the current source points to the right, indicating that the branch current flows from the direction of a toward b. U_ba is marked below in the figure, with a negative sign on the left side and a positive sign on the right side, therefore U_ba = V_b - V_a. Reasoning: It is known that U_ba = V_b - V_a = 10V, so V_b is 10V higher than V_a. The branch current is 1A, flowing from a to b through the 10Ω resistor, therefore the voltage drop on the resistor is IR = 1A × 10Ω = 10V, that is, the potential of the right-end node of the resistor is 10V lower than point a. Let the node between the resistor and the current source be x, then V_x = V_a - 10V, while V_b = V_a + 10V. Therefore the voltage across the two ends of the current source is V_b - V_x = (V_a + 10) - (V_a - 10) = 20V, and the right end b is at high potential. The 1A current in the current source flows from the left-end low-potential end to the right-end high-potential end, indicating that the current source supplies power outward, and its supplied power is 20V × 1A = 20W.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, if the voltage \(U_{ba} = 10\text{V}\), the power supplied by the 1A current source is ______ W.

method.method_draft: Let the series current be 1A from a to b, as shown by the current source arrow. From the text, U_ba = V_b - V_a = 10V. Across the 10Ω resistor with 1A left-to-right current, the voltage drop is IR = 10V, so the node between the resistor and current source is 10V below node a. Therefore the right terminal of the current source at b is 20V above its left terminal. Since the 1A current flows through the source from its lower-potential/negative side to its higher-potential/positive side, the current source delivers power P = 20V × 1A = 20W.

method.method_draft: Treat the whole a-b branch as a two-terminal element carrying 1A from a to b. Because U_ba = V_b - V_a = 10V, the branch voltage in the direction of the entering current at a is V_ab = -10V, so the whole branch absorbs P_branch = V_ab I = -10W, i.e. it supplies 10W externally. The resistor inside the branch absorbs P_R = I^2R = 1^2 × 10 = 10W. For the branch total to be -10W while the resistor absorbs +10W, the current source must have absorbed power P_s = -20W. Therefore the power supplied by the 1A current source is 20W.
